_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 49 (Jacob's blessings — the long poem). Saadia-specific moves throughout: v.5 'אלאת אלצ'לם' = 'instruments of injustice' for כלי חמס; v.6 'קלעו סורהא' = 'uprooted its wall' (interpretive); v.10 'קצ'יב אלמלך' = 'the staff of royalty' for שבט (Saadia interprets שילה as 'the one to whom it [the rule] belongs'); v.11 'גחאשה' = 'his foal'; v.16 'גמלה' סבט' = 'a whole tribe'; v.22 'אבן מת'מר' = 'fruit-bearing son' (etymologized rendering); v.25-26 the cluster of blessings rendered carefully.

translations.1: Then Jacob called for his sons, and said: 'Gather, that I may tell you what shall meet you in the end of days.
translations.2: Gather and hear this, O sons of Jacob; and listen to Israel your father.
translations.3: O Reuben, you are my firstborn — and my strength, and the first of my produce — preeminent in honor, and preeminent in might.
translations.4: And now — by an [unstable] flowing, you shall not be preeminent; since you went up to your father's bed — at that time, since my couch was profaned, you were cut off.
translations.5: Simeon and Levi are brothers — in instruments of injustice, their rulings.
translations.6: Into their counsel let my soul not enter; and in their assembly let my essence not be gathered. For in their wrath they slew a [whole] community, and at their pleasure they uprooted its wall.
translations.7: Cursed therefore is their wrath — how strong! — and their fury — how hard! I shall divide them in Jacob, and disperse them in Israel.
translations.8: And you, O Judah — your brothers shall make you their lord; and your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies; and your father's sons shall bow before you.
translations.9: You, O Judah, shall be as the cub of a lion — for you have delivered my son from being killed — which, when he crouches and lies down, like a lion or lioness, who shall rouse him?
translations.10: The staff of royalty shall not depart from Judah, nor the lawgiver from under his command — until he comes to whom it belongs; and to him shall the peoples be gathered.
translations.11: Binding to the vine his foal, and to the chosen-stock his she-ass's young; washing his garment in wine, and his robe in the blood of grapes.
translations.12: More dazzling are the eyes than wine, and whiter are the teeth than milk.
translations.13: And Zebulun shall dwell upon the shore of the sea, and upon its coast — ships; and the end of his border shall be by Sidon.
translations.14: And Issachar is like a separate-bodied [one] — crouching between the camps.
translations.15: Then he sees that rest is good, and the land is pleasant; and he stretches out his neck for carrying, and becomes like a tribute-paying servant.
translations.16: And Dan shall judge his people, as a whole tribe among the tribes of Israel.
translations.17: And Dan shall be like a serpent upon the way, and like a striker upon the path — biting the horse's heel, that its rider falls backward.
translations.18: He says: I hope for Your deliverance, O God.
translations.19: Gad — whatever troop musters against him, he shall pursue at their heels.
translations.20: And Asher — his food is rich; and he yields royal delicacies.
translations.21: Naphtali is like a doe sent forth — bringing back fine words.
translations.22: And Joseph is a fruit-bearing son — like a fruit-bearing bough by a spring of water, whose roots have spread over a wall.
translations.23: And the masters of arrows embittered him, and shot at him, and threatened him.
translations.24: But his bow remained firm in strength, and his arms were made strong, by the obedience to the Mighty One of Jacob; and from there — He shepherded the essence of Israel.
translations.25: Ask of your father's Power, that He may help you; and of the Sufficient One, that He may bless upon you — blessings of the sky from above, blessings of the deep crouching below, blessings of breasts and womb.
translations.26: And the blessings of your father shall be added to the blessings of my forefathers — up to what the bounds of eternity desire. May all be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.
translations.27: And Benjamin is like a tearing wolf — in the morning he eats spoil, and in the evening he divides plunder.'
translations.28: These are all the tribes of Israel — twelve; and this is what their father said to them, and blessed them. Each man according to his worth he blessed.
translations.29: Then he commanded them, and said to them: 'I am being gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers, in the cave which is in the field of Ephron the Hittite.
translations.30: It is the cave which is in the doubled field over against Mamre, in the land of Canaan — which Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial-place.
translations.31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.
translations.32: The field, and the cave which was in it, was bought from the sons of Heth.'
translations.33: And when Jacob had finished commanding his sons, he gathered his feet onto the bed; and he expired, and was gathered to his people.
